questions.question: Who is known as the "father of microbiology"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antonie van Leeuwenhoek**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek** (1632−1723) is universally recognized as the **Father of Microbiology** because he was the first person to observe and describe **microorganisms**.
 
• A **Dutch** scientist and businessman, he developed high-quality **single-lens microscopes** with magnification power exceeding **200 times**, which was far superior to the compound microscopes of the **17th century**.
 
• In **1674**, he discovered **protozoa**, and in **1676**, he became the first human to witness **bacteria**, which he initially described as **animalcules** in his letters to the **Royal Society of London**.
 
• His extensive research provided the first microscopic descriptions of **red blood cells**, **spermatozoa**, **yeast**, and the **capillary system**, effectively establishing the foundation for **microbiology** and **protozoology**.
 
• Unlike his contemporaries, Leeuwenhoek achieved exceptional clarity in his lenses, allowing him to visualize the **microscopic world** with a level of detail that would not be surpassed for over a century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Louis Pasteur**:

 
 
• Commonly referred to as the father of **modern microbiology** and **bacteriology**.
 
• He is famous for proving the **germ theory of disease** and developing the process of **pasteurization** to kill harmful microbes in food.
 
• He created vaccines for **rabies** and **anthrax**, significantly advancing the field of preventive medicine.
 
 
 
• **Robert Hooke**:
 
 
• An English scientist who, in **1665**, used a microscope to observe a thin slice of **cork** and coined the term **cell**.
 
• He published his findings in the landmark book **Micrographia**, which featured detailed illustrations of insects and plants.
 
 
 
• **Edward Jenner**:
 
 
• Regarded as the father of **immunology** for his pioneering work in **1796**.
 
• He developed the **smallpox vaccine**, the first successful vaccine in human history, by utilizing **cowpox** material to create immunity.

questions.question: Which of the following ozone-depleting substances (ODS) releases bromine atoms when exposed to ultraviolet (UV) radiation in the stratosphere?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Halons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Halons** are a specific class of **halogenated hydrocarbons** that contain **bromine**, along with **fluorine** and **carbon** atoms.
 
• In the Earth's **stratosphere**, these compounds are broken down by high-energy **ultraviolet (UV) radiation** in a process known as **photolysis** or photodissociation.
 
• This reaction results in the release of highly reactive **atomic bromine**, which acts as a powerful catalyst in the destruction of the **ozone layer**.
 
• Scientifically, **bromine** is significantly more destructive to **ozone (O₃)** than chlorine; it is estimated that a single bromine atom can be **40 to 100 times** more efficient at destroying ozone molecules than a single chlorine atom.
 
• Historically, **Halons** were extensively used in **fire suppression systems** and **portable fire extinguishers** because they are electrically non-conductive and leave no residue after application.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Ozone-Depleting Substances (ODS):**

 
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs):** These contain **chlorine**, fluorine, and carbon. When exposed to UV radiation, they release **chlorine atoms**, which are the primary drivers of ozone depletion in the polar regions.
 
• **Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs):** These were developed as transitional substitutes for CFCs. While they also release **chlorine**, they contain **hydrogen**, making them more likely to break down in the lower atmosphere before reaching the stratosphere.
 
• **Carbon tetrachloride (CCl₄):** A heavy, volatile liquid used historically as a **cleaning agent** and **refrigerant precursor**. It releases **chlorine atoms** upon UV exposure and has a high **Ozone Depletion Potential (ODP)**.
 
• **Montreal Protocol:** This 1987 international treaty mandates the phase-out of **Halons** and other ODS to facilitate the recovery of the **Earth's ozone shield**.

questions.question: Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for thinking?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fore-brain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fore-brain** (Prosencephalon) is the largest and most complex portion of the human brain, serving as the main site for **higher cognitive functions** and **abstract thinking**.
 
• It includes the **Cerebrum**, which is the specialized region responsible for **logical reasoning**, **intelligence**, **imagination**, and **decision-making**.
 
• The **Cerebral Cortex**, the outer layer of the fore-brain, processes sensory information from the eyes, ears, and skin to translate them into **conscious thoughts** and perceptions.
 
• Within the fore-brain, the **Frontal Lobe** plays a critical role in executive functions such as **problem-solving**, **planning**, and **voluntary muscle control**.
 
• The fore-brain also manages the storage of **long-term memory** and the interpretation of **language**, which are fundamental to the human thinking process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mid-brain**:

 
 
• Acts as a vital relay center for **visual and auditory impulses** between the hind-brain and fore-brain.
 
• Controls involuntary eye movements and the **pupillary reflex**, which adjusts the size of the pupil in response to light.
 
 
 
• **Hind-brain**:
 
 
• Consists of the **Cerebellum**, **Pons**, and **Medulla Oblongata**.
 
• The **Cerebellum** is responsible for maintaining **posture**, **equilibrium**, and **precision in voluntary movements**.
 
• The **Medulla Oblongata** controls essential life-sustaining involuntary activities like **heartbeat**, **blood pressure**, and **respiration**.
 
 
 
• **Spinal Cord**:
 
 
• A cylindrical bundle of nerve fibers that extends from the **Medulla** through the vertebral column.
 
• It acts as the primary pathway for transmitting signals between the brain and the body and coordinates **reflex actions** without direct brain involvement.

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Deputy Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu in September 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Udhayanidhi Stalin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Udhayanidhi Stalin** was officially appointed as the **Deputy Chief Minister** of **Tamil Nadu** on **September 28, 2024**, following a cabinet reshuffle recommended by Chief Minister **M.K. Stalin**.
 
• He becomes the third individual to hold the office of Deputy Chief Minister in Tamil Nadu, a position previously occupied by his father **M.K. Stalin** (2009–2011) and **O. Panneerselvam** (2017–2021).
 
• Prior to this elevation, he served as the **Minister for Youth Welfare and Sports Development**, a portfolio he continues to hold along with the newly assigned **Planning and Development** department.
 
• He is an elected member of the **Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly** representing the **Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni** constituency and is a key youth leader of the **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)** party.
 
• The swearing-in ceremony was conducted at **Raj Bhavan**, where Governor **R.N. Ravi** administered the oath of office to him and other newly inducted or reassigned ministers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **K. Palaniswami**:

 
 
• He is the former **Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu** (2017–2021) and currently serves as the **Leader of the Opposition** in the State Assembly.
 
• He is the **General Secretary** of the **All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK)**.
 
 
 
• **O. Panneerselvam**:
 
 
• A senior political figure who has served as the **Chief Minister** of Tamil Nadu multiple times and was the **Deputy Chief Minister** during the 2017–2021 tenure.
 
 
 
• **V. Senthil Balaji**:
 
 
• He was re-inducted into the **Tamil Nadu Cabinet** as the **Minister for Electricity, Non-Conventional Energy Development, Prohibition, and Excise** in September 2024.
 
• His re-induction followed his release from incarceration after the **Supreme Court** granted him bail in a money laundering case.

questions.question:
With respect to excretion in Human Beings, which of the following statement is correct?

I. Kidneys are located in the abdomen, one on either side of the backbone. II. Urine produced in the kidneys passes through the ureters into the urinary bladder.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The human **Excretory System** consists of a pair of **kidneys**, which are the primary filtration organs. These **bean-shaped** organs are located in the **abdominal cavity**, positioned retroperitoneally on either side of the **backbone** (vertebral column). *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• Once urine is produced in the **nephrons** of the kidneys through processes like **ultrafiltration** and **reabsorption**, it travels down through a pair of long, muscular tubes known as **ureters**. These tubes connect the kidneys to the **urinary bladder**, where urine is stored until it is released. *Hence, statement II is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of the Human Urinary System**:

 
 
• **Kidneys**: Responsible for removing **nitrogenous wastes** such as **urea** and **uric acid** from the blood. They maintain **osmoregulation** and **ionic balance**.
 
• **Nephron**: The basic **functional unit** of the kidney. Each kidney contains approximately 1 million nephrons that filter blood to form urine.
 
• **Urinary Bladder**: A distensible muscular organ that acts as a reservoir. It is under the control of the **nervous system**, allowing for voluntary control over **micturition** (urination).
 
• **Urethra**: The final muscular tube through which urine passes from the bladder to the exterior of the body.
 
 
 
• **Blood Supply**: Blood enters the kidneys via the **renal artery** and leaves via the **renal vein** after being filtered.

questions.question: Which of the following planet is fifth largest in size in our solar system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In terms of physical dimensions, **Earth** is the **fifth largest planet** in our **Solar System**. It follows the four giant planets: **Jupiter**, **Saturn**, **Uranus**, and **Neptune**.
 
• The descending order of planets by size (diameter) is **Jupiter** (largest), **Saturn**, **Uranus**, **Neptune**, **Earth**, **Venus**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** (smallest).
 
• **Earth** has an equatorial diameter of approximately **12,756 kilometers** (roughly **7,926 miles**), making it the largest of the four **terrestrial planets** (rocky planets).
 
• It is the **third planet** from the **Sun** and is the only known celestial body to support life, possessing a unique atmosphere and liquid water.
 
• The shape of the planet is not a perfect sphere but an **oblate spheroid** or **Geoid**, meaning it is slightly flattened at the **Poles** and bulging at the **Equator** due to its rotation.
 
• Therefore, **Earth** is the correct answer as it holds the fifth position in the size ranking of the eight major planets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mercury**:

 
 
• It is the **smallest planet** in the solar system, with a diameter of about **4,879 kilometers**.
 
• It is the closest planet to the **Sun** and lacks a significant atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Venus**:
 
 
• Ranking as the **sixth largest** planet, it is often referred to as **Earth's twin** due to its similar size and mass.
 
• It has a diameter of approximately **12,104 kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **Uranus**:
 
 
• It is the **third largest** planet in the solar system by diameter (about **50,724 kilometers**) and the **fourth largest** by mass.
 
• It is classified as an **Ice Giant** because it is mostly composed of elements heavier than hydrogen and helium, such as oxygen, carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur.

questions.question: Which of the following is an indigenous wind instrument, also known as 'Nayanam'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nadaswaram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nadaswaram** is a premier **double-reed wind instrument** originating from **South India**, and it is recognized as one of the world's loudest non-brass acoustic instruments.
 
• The instrument is popularly known as **Nayanam** or **Nagaswaram** in regional contexts, particularly in the state of **Tamil Nadu**, where it is a central part of the **Carnatic music** tradition.
 
• Structurally, the **Nadaswaram** consists of a long **conical tube** traditionally made from **Aacha wood** (hard ebony), featuring seven finger holes and a large, detachable **flaring bell** made of wood or metal.
 
• It is classified as an **aerophone** and uses a double reed called the **Seevali**, which is made from a type of marsh reed found in the **Kaveri River** delta.
 
• Culturally, it is revered as a **Mangala Vadya** (auspicious instrument) and is indispensable in **Hindu weddings**, **temple festivals**, and religious rituals across the **Southern Indian peninsula**.
 
• Historically, maestros like **Sheikh Chinna Moulana** and **T.N. Rajarathnam Pillai** have significantly elevated the status of this instrument in the global **classical music** arena.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gogona**:

 
 
• It is a traditional **Assamese** folk instrument made of bamboo, categorized as a type of **jaw harp** or **lamellophone**, typically played during the **Bihu festival**.
 
 
 
• **Timki**:
 
 
• A small **percussion instrument** or kettle drum used by tribal communities in **Central India**, often used to provide rhythmic accompaniment to **folk dances**.
 
 
 
• **Harmonium**:
 
 
• A **keyboard-based aerophone** that produces sound through free reeds; although ubiquitous in **Hindustani** and **Sufi** music today, it was introduced to India by **European missionaries** and is not an ancient indigenous invention.

questions.question: 'Tur', a cylindrical musical instrument made of clay with leather surfaces on both sides, is a type of ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tur** is a traditional **percussion instrument** extensively utilized in the folk music traditions of **Gujarat**, specifically among the **Dubla** and **Dhodia** tribal communities. It is defined by its **cylindrical body**, which is traditionally fashioned from **clay** or terracotta.
 
• As a classic example of a **Membranophone**, the **Tur** features **leather surfaces** or animal hides stretched across both ends of the cylinder. These membranes are struck manually to produce rhythmic sounds, which confirms its classification as a **Drum**.
 
• In Indian musicology, based on the **Natya Shastra**, instruments like the **Tur** are categorized as **Avanaddha Vadya**. This category encompasses all instruments where sound is generated by striking a stretched membrane.
 
• The instrument is central to **tribal dances** and social ceremonies, providing the primary rhythmic foundation for various cultural performances in Western India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harmonium**:

 
 
• A keyboard-based **reed organ** that produces sound by pushing air through metal reeds via manual **bellows**. It is classified as an **Aerophone**.
 
 
 
• **Cymbal**:
 
 
• Commonly referred to as **Manjira** or **Kantal** in India, these are **Idiophones** made of metal alloys that produce sound when two plates are struck together.
 
 
 
• **Guitar**:
 
 
• A **stringed instrument** or **Chordophone** where sound is produced by plucking or strumming strings over a soundboard or through electronic amplification.
 
 
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya** Context:
 
 
• Other notable instruments in this category include the **Tabla**, **Mrudangam**, and **Dholak**, all of which rely on **leather membranes** for sound production.

questions.question: The Shalimar Bagh in Jammu and Kashmir was built by ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jahangir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shalimar Bagh** is the largest **Mughal garden** in the **Kashmir Valley**, located on the northeast shore of the **Dal Lake** in **Srinagar**.
 
• It was built by the fourth Mughal Emperor **Jahangir** in the year **1619** as a summer retreat for his wife, **Empress Nur Jahan**.
 
• The garden is considered the high point of **Mughal horticulture** and is often referred to as the **Crown of Srinagar** or the **Garden of Bliss**.
 
• The layout follows the **Charbagh** architectural concept, which is a quadrilateral garden layout based on the four gardens of Paradise mentioned in the **Quran**.
 
• It is divided into three distinct terraces: the lowest was for the public (**Diwan-i-Aam**), the middle for the Emperor (**Diwan-i-Khas** or **Farah Baksh**), and the top terrace for the royal ladies (**Zenana** or **Faiz Baksh**).
 
• The garden features a central water channel known as the **Shah Nahar**, which is fed by the **Harwan garden** springs and flows through the terraces into the **Dal Lake**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babur:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the **Mughal Empire** and introduced the **Persian garden** style to India.
 
• His most famous garden is the **Aram Bagh** (originally **Bagh-i-Gul-Afshan**) located in **Agra**, built in **1528**.
 
 
 
• **Akbar:**
 
 
• He was responsible for building the **Naseem Bagh** in **Srinagar** in **1586**, which is the oldest Mughal garden in **Kashmir** and is famous for its massive **Chinar trees**.
 
 
 
• **Humayun:**
 
 
• Though he did not build famous gardens in Kashmir, his tomb in **Delhi**, commissioned by his wife **Bega Begum**, is a landmark example of a **garden-tomb** in India.
 
 
 
• **Shah Jahan:**
 
 
• He was the son of **Jahangir** and significantly extended **Shalimar Bagh** in **1630**.
 
• He also constructed the **Shalimar Gardens** in **Lahore** in **1641** and the **Chashme Shahi** garden in **Srinagar** in **1632**.

questions.question: Sachin Nag, an Asian games medallist is related to which of the following sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swimming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sachin Nag** (1920–1987) was a distinguished **Indian swimmer** who etched his name in sports history by winning the **first-ever gold medal** for India in the inaugural **Asian Games**.
 
• He achieved this historic milestone at the **1951 Asian Games** held in **New Delhi**, securing the gold medal in the **100-meter freestyle** swimming event.
 
• Apart from his prowess in competitive swimming, Nag was an exceptionally skilled **water polo** player, showcasing his versatility in aquatic sports.
 
• He represented India on the global stage at two **Olympic Games**, participating in the **1948 London Olympics** and the **1952 Helsinki Olympics** in both swimming and water polo disciplines.
 
• In the 1951 Asian Games, he also contributed to India's success by winning **bronze medals** in the **4×100-meter freestyle relay** and the **3×100-meter medley relay**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Aquatics and Asian Games**:

 
 
• The **1951 Asian Games** saw India finishing second in the overall medal tally, with swimming being a key contributor to the count.
 
• The **Swimming Federation of India (SFI)** is the national governing body responsible for the development and administration of swimming, diving, and water polo in the country.
 
• Other notable Indian swimmers who gained international acclaim include **Mihir Sen**, the first Indian to swim across the **English Channel** in 1958, and **Arati Saha**, the first Indian woman to achieve the same feat.
 
• In more recent history, **Virdhawal Khade** ended a 24-year medal drought for India in swimming at the Asian Games by winning a bronze in the 50m butterfly at the **2010 Guangzhou Games**.

questions.question:
In cricket which of the following cricket equipment is primarily made of wood?

I. Helmet II. Bat
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement I**: A **Helmet** is a critical piece of protective equipment used by batsmen, wicket-keepers, and close-in fielders to prevent head injuries. The outer shell is typically manufactured from high-impact synthetic materials such as **Carbon Fiber**, **Kevlar**, **Fibreglass**, or **ABS Plastic**, while the inner lining consists of **high-density foam** and the grille is made of **Steel** or **Titanium**. Wood is not used in its primary construction due to its inability to meet modern impact-resistance safety standards. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***
 
• **Statement II**: A **Bat** is the specialized equipment used by batsmen to hit the ball and is traditionally crafted from wood. The blade of a professional cricket bat is primarily made from **English Willow** (**Salix alba caerulea**) or **Kashmir Willow**, which are chosen for their unique properties of strength, compression resistance, and lightweight nature. The handle is usually made of **Cane** and **Rubber** to provide flexibility and shock absorption. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cricket Bat Wood Varieties**:

 
 
• **English Willow**: It is the standard for high-level international cricket, known for its **natural moisture** and **straight grains**, providing the best rebound qualities.
 
• **Kashmir Willow**: Primarily grown in **India**, it is tougher and heavier than its English counterpart, making it highly durable for recreational use.
 
• **Knocking-in**: This is a process where the wood fibers are compressed using a **wooden mallet** to prevent the bat from cracking upon impact with a **leather ball**.
 
 
 
• **Protective Gear Composition**:
 
 
• **Stumps and Bails**: These are also primarily made of wood, often using **Ash** or **Guava** wood for durability and weight.
 
• **Leg Guards (Pads)**: Constructed using **synthetic leather** (PVC or PU), **cane ribs**, and **internal foam** padding for protection.

questions.question:
Which of the following is an example of biotic factor responsible for the loss of grains in storage?

I. Inappropriate moisture II. Rodents
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biotic factors** refer to the living components or organisms in an ecosystem that influence or affect other organisms. In the context of **grain storage**, **rodents** such as rats and mice are living organisms that cause significant damage by consuming grains and contaminating them with their **excreta**, **urine**, and **hair**. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• **Abiotic factors** are the non-living chemical and physical parts of the environment. **Inappropriate moisture** levels (either too high or too low) represent a physical environmental condition. While moisture influences the survival of biotic factors, it is not a living organism itself. ***Hence, statement I is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biotic Factors** causing grain loss:

 
 
• **Insects:** Pests like the **Rice Weevil** and **Pulse Beetle** penetrate grain kernels, leading to weight loss and reduced nutritional value.
 
• **Microorganisms:** These include **Fungi** (molds) and **Bacteria** that cause discoloration, foul odors, and produce toxic substances like **Aflatoxins**.
 
• **Mites:** Microscopic organisms that thrive in high-humidity environments and damage the **grain germ**.
 
 
 
• **Abiotic Factors** causing grain loss:
 
 
• **Temperature:** Improper temperatures can lead to **thermal damage** and increase the **respiration rate** of the grains, causing them to lose dry matter.
 
• **Humidity:** High atmospheric humidity increases the **moisture content** of the seeds, making them susceptible to fungal growth and sprouting.
 
 
 
• Impact of these factors includes **degradation in quality**, **loss in weight**, **poor germinability**, and **discoloration** of produce, all of which lead to poor marketability.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is correct regarding poultry? I. Poultry farming is done to raise domestic fowls. II. Poultry production includes egg production and broiler production for poultry meat.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Poultry farming** is a specialized branch of **animal husbandry** dedicated to the rearing, breeding, and management of **domesticated fowls** or birds, primarily chickens, for economic purposes. **Hence, statement I is correct.**
 
• The industry is fundamentally structured into two primary streams: **egg production** and **meat production**, which utilize different specialized bird varieties to maximize yield and efficiency. **Hence, statement II is correct.**
 
• **Broilers** are specifically raised for **meat production**; they are bred for rapid growth and high feed conversion ratios, reaching market weight in a short period.
 
• **Layers** are domesticated birds maintained exclusively for **egg production**, requiring specific environmental conditions and nutritional management to sustain consistent laying cycles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nutritional Management**:

 
 
• **Broiler rations** are formulated with high **protein** and **fat** content, supplemented with essential vitamins like **Vitamin A** and **Vitamin K** to facilitate muscle development.
 
• **Layer rations** require balanced levels of **calcium** and **phosphorus** to ensure the formation of strong, high-quality eggshells.
 
 
 
• **Breeding Objectives**:
 
 
• Poultry programs often involve **cross-breeding** between indigenous breeds like **Aseel** and exotic breeds like **Leghorn**.
 
• Goals include improving **chick quality**, developing **dwarf broiler parents** for commercial chick production, and ensuring **summer adaptation capacity** or tolerance to high temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Disease Control**: Poultry are susceptible to various **viral, bacterial, and fungal diseases**, necessitating strict **sanitation**, **spraying of disinfectants**, and timely **vaccination** to prevent large-scale mortality.

questions.question: What is the primary function of plant cell wall?

options.text: To carry out photosynthesis in plants

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Provides structural strength to plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **plant cell wall** is a specialized, rigid outer layer positioned outside the **cell membrane**, serving as a defining feature of plant cells, fungi, and some algae.
 
• The primary chemical constituent of the cell wall is **cellulose**, a complex **polysaccharide** that provides high tensile and **structural strength** to the plant. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• Because plants lack a skeletal system like animals, the cell wall provides the necessary **rigidity** and framework required for plants to grow tall and resist **mechanical stress**.
 
• It maintains the **shape of the cell** and regulates **turgor pressure**, which is the internal pressure of the cell sap against the wall that keeps the plant **turgid** and upright.
 
• The cell wall acts as a **semi-permeable** barrier that prevents the cell from **osmotic lysis** (bursting) when placed in a **hypotonic environment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Components**:

 
 
• **Cellulose Microfibrils**: Long chains of **glucose** that form the primary structural skeleton of the wall.
 
• **Hemicellulose and Pectin**: These molecules cross-link cellulose fibers and form the **middle lamella**, acting as a glue between adjacent cells.
 
• **Lignin**: Found in secondary walls, it provides extra **stiffness** and **waterproofing** in woody tissues.
 
 
 
• **Functional Distinctions**:
 
 
• **Photosynthesis and Food Synthesis**: These metabolic functions are carried out by **chloroplasts**, which contain the green pigment **chlorophyll**. The cell wall does not contain the machinery for **carbon fixation**.
 
• **Cell Division**: This process is controlled by the **nucleus** and **cytoskeletal elements** like **microtubules**. While a **cell plate** is formed during cytokinesis to create a new wall, the wall itself does not facilitate the division.

questions.question: In which event did Avinash Sable win a gold medal at the Asian Games 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Steeplechase**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Avinash Mukund Sable** is a distinguished Indian **track and field athlete** who specialized in the **3000 meters steeplechase** during the **Asian Games 2023**.
 
• In the **19th edition** of the **Asian Games** held in **Hangzhou, China**, Sable clinched the **gold medal**, marking a historic achievement for Indian athletics.
 
• He became the **first Indian male athlete** to secure a gold medal in this specific discipline at the **Asian Games**, showcasing India's growing dominance in long-distance obstacle racing.
 
• Sable completed the race with a timing of **8:19.50**, which established a new **Asian Games Record**, breaking the previous mark held by Iran's Hossein Keyhani.
 
• His performance was characterized by an aggressive start where he maintained a significant lead over the rest of the field throughout the **3000m** course.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Event Characteristics:**

 
 
• The **3000m Steeplechase** is an intense **obstacle race** consisting of **28 fixed barriers** and **7 water jumps**.
 
• Athletes must possess a combination of **endurance**, **hurdling technique**, and the ability to maintain pace after landing in water pits.
 
 
 
• **Athlete Profile:**
 
 
• **Avinash Sable** hails from the **Beed district** of **Maharashtra** and is a serving **Naib Subedar** in the **5 Mahar Regiment** of the **Indian Army**.
 
• He also won a **silver medal** in the **5000 meters** event at the same **Asian Games**, finishing with a time of **13:21.09**.
 
• Prior to this, he gained international acclaim by winning a **silver medal** at the **2022 Commonwealth Games** in **Birmingham**, where he famously challenged the long-standing Kenyan monopoly in the event.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Badminton:** While India won several medals in badminton (including a historic gold in Men's Doubles), Sable is purely a track athlete.
 
• **Golf:** India's **Aditi Ashok** won a silver medal in this category, but it is unrelated to Sable's field of expertise.
 
• **Cycling:** This sport involves track and road races on bicycles, whereas Sable competes in **athletics** (running).

questions.question: Which of the following indices is NOT published by World Economic Forum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human Development Index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a tool developed by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**, not the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**. It was first introduced in **1990**.
 
• The index was pioneered by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian Nobel laureate **Amartya Sen** to shift the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies.
 
• The **HDI** is a composite statistic that aggregates three basic dimensions of human development: **Long and healthy life** (measured by life expectancy at birth), **Knowledge** (measured by mean and expected years of schooling), and a **Decent standard of living** (measured by **GNI per capita** at Purchasing Power Parity).
 
• In contrast, the **World Economic Forum** is an international organization for public-private cooperation based in **Cologny, Switzerland**, and is responsible for the other indices mentioned in the options.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Gender Gap Index**:

 
 
• This index was first published in **2006** by the **World Economic Forum**.
 
• It benchmarks national gender gaps on **economic participation**, **educational attainment**, **health and survival**, and **political empowerment**.
 
 
 
• **Global Competitiveness Index**:
 
 
• An annual report published by the **WEF** since **1979** that ranks countries based on the **Global Competitiveness Report**.
 
• It assesses the **microeconomic** and **macroeconomic** foundations of national competitiveness through **12 pillars**, including infrastructure, **technological readiness**, and **innovation**.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transition Index (ETI)**:
 
 
• Published by the **WEF** in collaboration with **Accenture**, it tracks the progress of nations toward **energy system performance** and **transition readiness**.
 
• The framework is based on the **energy triangle**, which balances **environmental sustainability**, **energy security**, and **economic development**.
 
 
 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF)**:
 
 
• Founded in **1971** by **Klaus Schwab**, the **WEF** is famous for its annual meeting in **Davos**.
 
• Other major reports published by **WEF** include the **Global Risks Report** and the **Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Report**.
